sections.heading: Scam and Account Protection
paragraph: Clients often contact us after a suspicious pop-up, phone call, text message, email, or account warning.
items: Fake virus alerts that display a support phone number
Calls pretending to come from a bank, technology company, retailer, or government agency
Requests for gift cards, wire transfers, cryptocurrency, passwords, or account codes
Remote-access software installed at the request of an unknown caller

faq.question: Do you provide in-home service throughout The Villages?
faq.answer: Yes. We provide on-site service throughout The Villages and nearby communities. Arranged pickup and drop-off may also be available when it fits the work better.

faq.question: Can you help remotely without visiting first?
faq.answer: Plan-based remote support requires an in-person enrollment visit. Online training and tutoring are separate services and do not require the Remote Support Plan.

faq.question: A pop-up says my computer is infected and tells me to call. What should I do?
faq.answer: Do not call the number or allow anyone to connect to the computer. Close the browser if possible. If someone already connected, disconnect the computer from the internet and turn it off, then contact us.

faq.question: Someone called claiming to be my bank or a technology company. How can I verify the call?
faq.answer: End the call and contact the organization through a trusted phone number on its official website, your statement, or the back of your card. Do not use a number provided by the caller.

faq.question: Do I need to be comfortable with technology?
faq.answer: No. We work at your pace, explain each step in plain English, and can write down important instructions when helpful.

faq.question: How much does service cost?
faq.answer: The cost depends on the work. We explain the expected price before service begins and discuss any additional work with you first.
